title: V4/TEO/FEF/PFC O++ restriction passes a causal RRRR-vs-RXRR divergence test; excluded areas fail it
notes: Hamm's argument (2026-08-17, verbatim): the subject cannot predict whether a given trial omits or when (e.g. AAXB is not foreseeable from AAAB's fixed timing), and no neuron anywhere can register 'the expected stimulus failed to appear' faster than the visual system's own minimum latency (~40ms) after the expected onset. Any activity that already differs between an omission trial and a real-stimulus trial BEFORE that floor has no possible causal source in the omission -- it is ordinary trial-timing-locked or stimulus-offset activity, not an omission response. Hamm's specific hypothesis: 'O++' candidates outside V4/TEO/FEF/PFC are slow-offset units (trailing decay of the response to the PRECEDING real stimulus), not genuine omission-selective units.

Test performed: compute_population_psth_multi_condition (fig03_unit_census.py, reused unmodified) computing per-area, per-unit PSTHs for RRRR (real stimulus at p2) and RXRR (omission at p2) on the SAME units, SAME absolute p1-aligned trial-time axis, for the r>=0.65 O+/O*+ candidate pool (grand_oplus_units.csv, deduplicated on unit identity). p2 onset = 1031ms (jnwb.unit_classification.EPOCH_ONSETS_MS); causal floor = 1071ms (+40ms). Figure: artifacts/.lab/diag_oplus_causality_test_rrrr_vs_rxrr_20260817.png.

RESULT, V4/TEO/FEF/PFC (the confirmed-O++ area set): all four areas show RRRR and RXRR traces closely overlapping BEFORE the causal floor (as required -- the unit cannot yet know its condition), then cleanly and consistently DIVERGING after it, with RXRR sustaining an elevation RRRR does not show for the remainder of the window. This is the correct causal signature of a genuine differential response to the omission.

RESULT, V1 (excluded area): the OPPOSITE pattern, not merely a weaker one. RRRR shows a sharp, fast (~50ms-latency) transient spike right after p2 onset -- an ordinary stimulus-evoked visual response -- while RXRR shows no corresponding spike and stays lower. Population-average V1 'O+' candidates are not elevated by the omission at all; they are simply units that respond normally when a real stimulus is present and don't when it's absent. The per-unit correlation-based selection that flagged these as 'O+' candidates must be picking out something the population average does not show, consistent with the already-diagnosed contamination mechanism (bug-oplus-candidate-pool-suppressed-unit-contamination-20260817.json) -- the template-correlation gate rewards a unit's own RELATIVE epoch shape, not a genuine RRRR-vs-omission difference.

RESULT, V2/V3/MT (excluded areas): no clean post-floor divergence -- RRRR and RXRR traces overlap heavily with wide, mutually-overlapping SEM bands throughout. Whatever pushes their candidates' correlation above 0.65 is not a reproducible population-level differential response either.

REPLICATED 2026-08-17 at p3 (RRXR) and p4 (RRRX), one additional NWB pass covering all 4 conditions x full trial window at once (compute_population_psth_multi_condition called ONCE, sliced per slot -- not rerun per slot). Figures: diag_oplus_causality_test_p2_20260817.png, _p3_..., _p4_.... Same pattern holds at every slot: V4/TEO/FEF/PFC overlap pre-floor and diverge cleanly post-floor; V1 shows the reverse (sharp RRRR transient, flat RXRR/RRXR/RRRX) at every slot; V2/V3/MT stay noisy/overlapping at every slot. Not a p2-specific artifact.

Hamm's sharper O++ criterion, applied and checked (verbatim): '...if and only if their spiking peaks at after onset of omission and comes down not sharply when next stimulus comes (if comes down sharply, it is evidence that it is slow S-/S-- rather than a O++)'. Checked directly at p2 and p3 (both have a within-trial next-real-stimulus line to test against; p4 is the last slot, no next-trial stimulus to check within this trial). At both p2 and p3, V4/TEO/FEF/PFC's omission trace does NOT cliff-drop at the next-stimulus line -- it stays elevated smoothly through it and only gradually reconverges with RRRR afterward. This satisfies Hamm's own criterion for genuine O++ (peaks after onset, gradual not sharp decay) and argues against the slow-offset-S-/S-- explanation specifically for these four areas.

This is DESCRIPTIVE (population-average traces, small n in several areas -- V1 n=7, V2 n=7, V3 n=8, MT n=5) and a visual/qualitative read of the trace shape and decay slope, not a formal statistic. It is nonetheless a real, principled, causally-motivated basis for the V4/TEO/FEF/PFC area restriction that goes beyond 'Hamm requested it' -- the restricted areas are exactly the ones whose population response passes a causality-respecting divergence test AND the peaks-after/decays-gradually criterion at every slot tested, while the most clearly excluded area (V1) fails the divergence test in the informative, backwards direction (real-stimulus response, not omission response) at every slot too.
issues: Still not a formal statistic (e.g. a permutation test on divergence-onset latency, or a quantified decay-slope comparison at the next-stimulus line) -- currently a visual/descriptive read of the population trace at all three slots, appropriate for a diagnostic but not for a manuscript claim without a proper test.

Does not yet directly link individual V1/V2/V3/MT candidate units back to their own S-/S-- legacy flags or per-unit decay kinetics to confirm the slow-offset-unit mechanism at the single-unit level -- this node supports the AREA-level population-average pattern, not yet the specific unit-level causal story Hamm's criterion is ultimately about (a per-unit peak-timing/decay-sharpness classifier, not just a population-average read).

plan.falsifier: Would be strengthened to confirmed by: (1) DONE -- replicated the RRRR-vs-{RXRR,RRXR,RRRX} divergence pattern at all three omission slots, same pattern every time; (2) a formal test of divergence-onset latency AND decay-slope-at-next-stimulus per area/unit, with the pre-registered prediction that V4/TEO/FEF/PFC diverge only after the +40ms causal floor and decay gradually, and the excluded areas either don't diverge credibly or decay sharply; (3) linking excluded-area candidate units individually to their legacy S-/S-- flags and per-unit decay kinetics to directly test the slow-offset-unit hypothesis at the unit level, not just the population-average level -- this would let the 'peaks after onset, decays gradually' rule become an actual per-unit inclusion criterion rather than a population-level visual check.

verification.verdict: PROVISIONAL. Real, reproducible pattern from a properly controlled comparison (same units, same axis, all four conditions from one spike-time pass), replicated identically at all three omission slots. Strong support for the area restriction and for Hamm's slow-offset-unit hypothesis on V1 specifically, and V4/TEO/FEF/PFC additionally satisfy Hamm's own peaks-after/decays-gradually criterion at every slot checked. Not yet a formal statistic and not yet confirmed at the individual-unit level.
